name: iSimangaliso and St Lucia
tagline: A vast wetland and coastal park of estuaries, hippos, crocodiles, forested dunes, coral reefs and turtle beaches, with rhinos at Hluhluwe–iMfolozi close by.
highlight: A boat cruise on the St Lucia estuary at sunset, surrounded by hippos and the sound of fish eagles.
shortDescription: South Africa's first UNESCO World Heritage Site: hippo and crocodile cruises on the St Lucia estuary, the beaches of Cape Vidal, diving at Sodwana Bay, turtle nesting, whales and nearby big-game parks.
metaDescription: An iSimangaliso and St Lucia travel guide: estuary boat cruises with hippos and crocodiles, Cape Vidal, Sodwana Bay diving, turtle nesting, Hluhluwe–iMfolozi rhinos, best time, malaria and a three-day plan.
nearestAirport: Richards Bay (RCB) or Durban King Shaka (DUR), about 2.5 to 3 hours by road
knownFor: Hippos, crocodiles, wetlands, beaches, turtles, snorkelling

intro: iSimangaliso Wetland Park, on the north-east coast of KwaZulu-Natal, stretches for about 220 km along the Indian Ocean, from the Mozambique border to Maphelane. Its name means miracle and wonder in Zulu, and it was South Africa's first UNESCO World Heritage Site, inscribed in 1999. The park protects a mosaic of habitats, including coral reefs, long beaches, coastal forest, dunes, lakes and swamps, and it is home to hippos, crocodiles, elephants, rhinos, leopards, turtles, whales, dolphins and hundreds of species of bird.

The centre of the park is Lake St Lucia, Africa's largest estuarine lake, and the small town of St Lucia, at its mouth, where hippos occasionally wander at night and boat trips leave to see them and the crocodiles. To the east, a sandy road leads through coastal forest to Cape Vidal, with warm-water reefs and beaches, and further north Sodwana Bay is a top diving destination, while Kosi Bay and the Maputaland coast have lakes and turtle nesting beaches. Leatherback and loggerhead turtles nest on the beaches from November to January.

Nearby, Hluhluwe–iMfolozi Park, one of the oldest game reserves in Africa, has the Big Five and is known for its white rhino conservation success. Together, they make a rewarding trip for wildlife lovers who want a mix of bush and beach. The region is a malaria area, and it is best visited in the drier winter months.

whyVisit.intro: iSimangaliso combines beach, wetland and bush wildlife, with a relaxed atmosphere and good value.

points.title: Hippos and crocodiles
points.text: Estuary cruises get close to some of the biggest hippo populations in Africa.

points.title: Beaches and reefs
points.text: Warm water, coral, snorkelling and diving, without the crowds.

points.title: Turtles and whales
points.text: Nesting turtles from November to January, and humpback whales from June to November.

points.title: Big-game nearby
points.text: Hluhluwe–iMfolozi and other reserves have rhinos, lions and elephants.

points.title: Birdlife
points.text: Over 500 species, including fish eagles and pelicans.

attractionsIntro: The park has several areas, and most visitors base themselves in St Lucia town.

attractions.name: St Lucia estuary boat cruise

image.file: File:Hippo (Hippopotamus amphibius) family resting on the shores of Lake St Lucia .. (31656974747).jpg
image.alt: A family of hippos resting on the shore of Lake St Lucia

attractions.text: A two-hour boat trip up the estuary, where you can see hippos, crocodiles, fish eagles and other birdlife from close range.

attractions.name: Cape Vidal

image.alt: The long sandy beach at Cape Vidal in iSimangaliso

attractions.text: A beach and camp on the coast, about 30 km from St Lucia, with reefs for snorkelling, a lookout for whales and a wildlife-rich drive through forest and grassland.

attractions.name: Sodwana Bay
attractions.text: One of South Africa's top diving spots, with warm water and reef fish, about 1.5 hours north of St Lucia.

attractions.name: Hluhluwe–iMfolozi Park
attractions.text: One of the oldest protected areas in Africa, established in 1895, with the Big Five and one of the best places to see white and black rhinos.

attractions.name: Turtle nesting beaches
attractions.text: Leatherback and loggerhead turtles come ashore to nest on the beaches of Maputaland, and guided night trips are available from November to January.
attractions.tip: Book a guided tour, and follow the rules.

attractions.name: Kosi Bay
attractions.text: A remote set of lakes and channels on the Mozambique border, with traditional fish traps and pristine beaches.

thingsToDoIntro: Water and wildlife activities fill the days.

thingsToDo.title: Take a hippo and crocodile cruise
thingsToDo.text: See hippos and crocs at close range on the estuary.

thingsToDo.title: Go on a game drive at Hluhluwe–iMfolozi
Watch whales
thingsToDo.text: Humpback whales pass from June to November.

foodIntro: Food in St Lucia is casual, with seafood and braai.

foods.name: Bunny chow
foods.text: Curry in a bread loaf, from Durban.

accommodation.intro: Stay in St Lucia town, or in a lodge nearer the park.

areas.name: Cape Vidal and park camps
areas.text: Cabins and campsites in the park.

gettingThere.intro: St Lucia is about 250 km north of Durban.

options.text: About 2.5 to 3 hours on the N2.
options.detail: Hire a car at the airport.

options.text: About 7 to 8 hours by road, or fly to Durban.

gettingAround.intro: A car is best, and the park's sand roads need care.

options.text: Tarred roads to Cape Vidal and Hluhluwe.

bestTime.headline: April–October
bestTime.summary: iSimangaliso has a subtropical climate, with hot, humid summers and mild, dry winters.

seasons.text: Hot and humid, with turtles nesting and rain.
Mild and dry, with whales and good game viewing.

bestTime.avoid: January and February for heat, humidity and malaria risk.

tipsIntro: A few tips help you stay safe.
tips: Do not walk around St Lucia at night, when hippos come ashore.
Never swim in the lake or estuary, where there are crocodiles.
Check malaria advice and take precautions.
Book turtle tours, cruises and camps in advance.
Take binoculars, a hat and sunscreen.
Carry cash for park entry fees.

faq.q: How many days do you need in iSimangaliso?
What is the best time to visit?
faq.a: April to October, with turtles from November to January.

faq.q: Can I swim at the beach?
faq.a: At some beaches, such as Cape Vidal, with care. Never swim in the lake.
Yes, if you follow wildlife safety rules.
